# Yes, the cable can limit charging speed

Charging runs at the lowest power that the charger, the device, and the cable all support.

## What the ratings mean
- **60W cable:** 20V at 3A. A 60W cable can't carry a 100W charger's full output.
- **100W cable:** 20V at 5A. It needs an e-marker chip (the cable's built-in "ID" that tells the charger it's safe to send 5A). This is the older tier, and the [USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector) no longer certifies 100W cables.
- **240W cable:** 48V at 5A, the Extended Power Range (EPR) tier. It requires an e-marker, and USB-IF requires the 240W logo.

According to [UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations), USB-IF discontinued certification of 100W USB-C cables on December 22, 2021. Certified USB-C to USB-C cables now come in only two power ratings, 60W and 240W. Plenty of uncertified 100W cables are still sold, and many work fine.

Higher voltages (28V, 36V, 48V) are what enable 140W, 180W, and 240W, per the [USB-IF Power Delivery page](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd). Your charger and device must also support those levels. A 240W cable won't make a 65W laptop charge faster.

## How to check yours
- Look for a 60W or 240W logo on the cable or packaging. USB-IF requires certified cables to carry one.
- If there's no marking, assume 60W or less.
- Compare your device's wattage (usually on its charger or spec sheet) to the cable's rating.

## Which one you need
- **Phones, tablets, and most small laptops (up to 60W):** a 60W cable is fine.
- **Laptops that draw 61-100W:** use a 100W (5A) or 240W cable.
- **Laptops or devices above 100W:** use a 240W cable.

## One budget option
If you need a 100W cable, the [Baseus USB-C to USB-C Cable, 100W](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w) is $9.99 for 1 m (listed price on 2026-10-21; $12.99 for 2 m, $16.99 for 3 m). It is e-marked at 5A, per the [product listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w). Caveats from that listing:
- It supports USB 2.0 data only (480 Mbps) and no video output, so it isn't suited to monitors or fast file transfers.
- It isn't rated for 140W or 240W.
- Baseus says it isn't supported for iPad Pro charging.

That buy link is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays the site a commission at no cost to you. The listing doesn't say whether this cable is USB-IF certified.
